summary:
WHERE IS THE ECLIPSING PAIR? It is within about 1.5" of the G star, most likely at about 0.5-1".

TESS:
- The raw PRF difference-image offsets (2-7") are a TESS optics artefact, not a position. Every sector's offset points radially away from that camera's boresight, with tangential components near zero, even though the sky direction of the boresight changes between sectors (PA 328-354 deg for S1/S28/S68/S95, 140 deg for S105, 46 deg for S106).
- I measured TESS lateral colour directly with field stars in 11 full frames from all six sectors. Redder stars appear displaced away from the boresight by about 75-86 mpx per mag of BP-RP; the relation steepens for red colours and has no tangential part. The eclipsed light is M-dwarf red, so its PRF centroid is pushed outward.
- One fixed sky position cannot explain the six sectors (chi2 = 265.5/22).
- 'Source on the G star plus a colour shift' fits well (chi2 = 21.1/22, empirical p = 0.51).
- With a free offset as well: delta = (-0.25 ± 0.18, +0.51 ± 0.26)", |delta| = 0.57", PA about 334 deg. delta = 0 is allowed (empirical p = 0.06).
- Injection-recovery with the target's own image (500 fake-epoch trials per sector and type, at 0/1/3/5") shows the pipeline is unbiased to about 0.2-0.5", with calibrated scatter of 0.4-0.8" (deep) and 0.8-1.35" (shallow) per axis.
- Empirical tail tests: a source at ≥1.5" is rejected at p = 0.0025, and at ≥2" in 0 of 2000 simulations (Gaussian chi2 change 31). All resolved Gaia neighbours are excluded.
- The fitted colour shifts imply the deep-eclipse light has BP-RP_eff ≈ 2.2 (about M1-M2 V) and the shallow-eclipse light is redder (≳ 2.8). That ordering is what an M-dwarf eclipsing pair predicts.

Gaia DR3:
- Only two diagnostics are abnormal: ipd_frac_multi_peak = 41 and 100% of BP/RP transits flagged as blended. AEN, RUWE, harmonic amplitude and BP/RP excess are typical of field stars.
- I cross-matched about 25,000 SOAR speckle rows to Gaia. The combination (fmp 28-56, RUWE < 1.4, BP-blend ≥ 0.8) occurs in 2/1464 speckle-single stars (0.14%) and only for companions at about 0.5-1.1" (16-84%: 0.53-1.06") with ΔI ≈ 1.6-3.9.
- The harmonic phase is weakly informative at this amplitude.

Archival imaging:
- DES/Legacy Survey: saturated. VHS J: saturated (flagged).
- SkyMapper short frames are unsaturated (FWHM 1.5-2.8"). With injection calibration they exclude a companion at ≥1.5" with Δi ≲ 3, but are blind below about 0.75".
- The VHS Ks catalogue shows a mild elongation excess (ellipticity 0.051 vs 0.019-0.031 for five comparable stars, along the PSF PA). A simple moment argument (catalogue level only; images unreachable) gives q(1-q)s² ≲ 0.03 arcsec², i.e. s ≲ 0.5" if ΔKs ≤ 2. This suggests the companion is closer than about 0.6" or fainter in Ks than about 2.5.

Together these support a bound hierarchical triple: an M-dwarf eclipsing binary about 0.5-1" (about 150-300 AU projected at 297 pc) from the G star. A chance-aligned background star bright enough to host the eclipses has about 6e-4 expected sources within 1.42".

conclusions.claim: The eclipsing source is NOT at the sky positions given by raw TESS PRF difference images; those 2-7" offsets (including earlier 'within 3-4"' TESScut results) are a TESS lateral-colour artefact.
conclusions.evidence: In all 6 sectors (3 cameras/CCD orientations), deep and shallow offsets point radially away from the camera boresight with tangential components ≤ 0.6" (deep). No single sky position fits (chi2 = 265.5/22). Field stars in 11 full frames show the same effect: redder stars displaced outward by 66-86 mpx/mag, with no tangential term. Injecting the target's own (G-coloured) image at fake epochs recovers 0" to within 0.2-0.5".

conclusions.claim: After modelling the colour shift, the eclipsing source is consistent with the G-star position and lies within about 1.5" of it; separations ≥ 2" and all resolved Gaia neighbours (18.7", 44.9", 47.3", 54.8") are excluded.
conclusions.evidence: Model M1 (on target + colour shift) chi2 21.1/22, empirical p = 0.51. M2 gives δ = (-0.25 ± 0.18, +0.51 ± 0.26)", stable across 16 variants. Empirical tails: 1.5" p = 0.0025; 2.0" 0/2000 (chi2 change 31); 3" chi2 change 90. The colour-free tangential fit agrees.

conclusions.claim: The best TESS position is about 0.5" NNW (PA about 313-343 deg) of the G star, but an exactly coincident source is allowed; eastern and southern positions beyond about 0.4" are disfavoured.
conclusions.evidence: |δ| = 0.57", 2.4 sigma from 0 (empirical p = 0.062); chi2 change ≥ 17 at PA 94-108 deg for ≥ 0.4"; western PA 274-288 deg allowed at ≤ 0.5-0.6" (chi2 change 4-6).

conclusions.claim: The eclipsed light is M-dwarf red, with the shallow-eclipse light redder than the deep-eclipse light, as expected for a cool pair where the shallow eclipse hides the cooler star.
conclusions.evidence: The fitted radial colour shifts (-2.98 ± 0.26" deep, -5.53 ± 0.43" shallow) match field stars with BP-RP ≈ 2.2 (deep) and ≳ 2.8 (shallow) on the lateral-colour curve. The two M dwarfs measured agree with giants of the same colour. A K7 primary (BP-RP 1.85) would give about -1.9", about 3 sigma short of the deep value unless limb reddening matters.

conclusions.claim: Gaia DR3 strongly indicates an unresolved companion at about 0.5-1.1" with ΔI about 1.6-3.9.
conclusions.evidence: fmp = 41 together with 100% BP/RP blended transits (fmp 28-56, RUWE < 1.4, blend ≥ 0.8) occurs in 2/1464 speckle-single stars (0.14%) versus about 30% of speckle binaries at 0.8-1.3" with ΔI 2.5-4.5. All six matched binaries span 0.27-1.10" (16-84%: 0.53-1.06"). Other Gaia diagnostics are normal (58th-71st percentiles).

conclusions.claim: The Gaia harmonic phase gives only a weak PA hint (PA ≈ 108 or 288 deg); combined with TESS, only the western branch survives.
conclusions.evidence: The empirical relation phase ≈ PA + 90 is tight only for amplitude > 0.05. At the target's 0.029, 40-50% of binaries fall within ±30 deg (random 33%). Singles have a median amplitude of 0.018 and an 84th percentile of 0.039, so the target's amplitude is not unusual.

conclusions.claim: Seeing-limited imaging cannot see the companion at the expected separation. SkyMapper excludes ≥ 1.5" companions with Δi ≲ 3. The VHS Ks catalogue morphology hints the companion is closer than about 0.6" or faint in Ks (ΔKs ≳ 2.5) if at 0.7-1".
conclusions.evidence: DES/Legacy Survey saturated (flags, 27" FWHM, mags 3 mag too faint) and VHS J flagged saturated. SkyMapper injection recovery: 75-100% at 2" with Δm ≤ 3.5 and 50-100% at 1.5" with Δm ≤ 3 in the best frames; blind at ≤ 0.75". VHS Ks ellipticity 0.051 vs 0.019-0.031 for comparison stars; moment bound q(1-q)s² ≲ 0.03 arcsec².

conclusions.claim: The earlier rough estimate (K7+M2, companion at about 1-1.8") should be revised: separation about 0.4-1.1" (most likely about 0.5-0.9") and a primary cooler than K7 (about M0-M2).
conclusions.evidence: TESS excludes > 1.5" at p = 0.0025. SkyMapper excludes ≥ 1.5" for Δi ≲ 3. Gaia-matched binaries have 84th-percentile separation 1.06". The VHS moment bound and the colour levers point the same way.

implications_bound_vs_background:
The background interpretation is disfavoured.

1. **Position.** The eclipsing source lies within about 1.4" (3 sigma) of the G star, with the best fit 0.57" away and δ = 0 allowed. Only about 6e-4 unrelated stars bright enough to host the eclipses (G < 17.5) are expected within that radius, or 1.5e-3 down to G < 19.5. For comparison, a bound companion at 100-400 AU around a solar-type star has an a priori probability of order 5-10%.

2. **Gaia.** Gaia independently requires an unresolved companion at about 0.5-1.1" with ΔI about 1.6-3.9. That signature appears in only 0.14% of speckle-single stars. The simplest reading is that this companion is the eclipsing binary itself.

3. **Colour.** The eclipsed light has the colours of M dwarfs (deep BP-RP_eff ≈ 2.2, shallow redder). That fits a cool, low-mass EB bound to a 1 Msun G star at 297 pc. It does not fix the distance on its own.

Taken together: a likely hierarchical triple, with an M-dwarf EB (P = 1.3037 d) about 0.5-1" from the G star (about 150-330 AU projected). A chance-aligned background EB would need to land within about 1.4" (a probability of about 1e-3) and also produce the Gaia IPD signature. It cannot be formally excluded without high-resolution imaging plus RVs or colours of the companion.

**Recommended decisive test:** SOAR/Gemini speckle or AO imaging (I or K band) to resolve the companion at about 0.4-1.1". A WNW-to-NNW position (PA about 280-340 deg) would be consistent with all the weak PA hints. Then multi-colour eclipse depths, or a spectrum of the companion, to confirm it is the EB and that its photometric distance matches 297 pc.
caveats:
1. **The TESS position depends on the lateral-colour model.** The colour shift is modelled as radial, with per-sector strength from field stars. Variants of that scaling move δ by ≤ 0.25", and the colour-free tangential fit agrees. Non-radial colour terms are measured to be ≤ 5 mpx/mag and are included. Any residual camera- or CCD-specific chromatic behaviour beyond this could bias δ at the ~0.2" level.
2. **The red end of the colour calibration is thin.** It rests on about 26 unique red giants and only 2 M dwarfs. The shallow-eclipse colour (≳ 2.8, best ≈ 3.6) is an extrapolation. Chromatic limb darkening in grazing eclipses makes the eclipsed light somewhat redder than the disk-integrated star, so the BP-RP_eff values are upper bounds on the true stellar colours by maybe 0.05-0.15 mag.
3. **One PRF version throughout.** The SPOC start_s0004 PRF was used for S28-S106 and start_s0001 for S1. Empirical-image and PRF-model injections agree, so PRF mismatch is negligible for a source of the target's colour.
4. **How the injection noise was drawn.** Each injection used one fake window per eclipse epoch, but windows from neighbouring phases overlap in time. Empirical tail probabilities are limited to about 5e-4 by 2000 simulations. Beyond that I quote Gaussian chi2 changes, which is reasonable since the noise is near-Gaussian (excess kurtosis between -0.17 and +0.26; tail fractions match 0.0027).
5. **Speckle sample biases.** The calibration sample mixes TESS hosts (Ziegler) and Hipparcos-like stars (Tokovinin, Mason). Δm is mostly I-band, while Gaia sees G. Speckle-'single' stars can hide companions beyond the speckle limits. Primaries were assigned as the brightest Gaia source within 2.5" of the speckle position. Only 6 binaries match the full signature, so the separation and contrast ranges are coarse. The BP/RP 'blended' flag is interpreted empirically, not from documented internals.
6. **VHS evidence is catalogue-level only.** VSA images were unreachable (port 8080 timed out; HTTPS certificate mismatch), and full ESO tiles are too large. The ellipticity argument assumes CASU unweighted isophotal moments and compares against 5 bright stars. The target's core may be in the nonlinear regime. The PA convention of KsPA was not verified, so treat the VHS bound as indicative.
7. **SkyMapper null sample.** The comparison stars are 5-20 times fainter than the target, so the null test uses injections into the target itself. Frames differ in seeing (1.46-2.84"); the quoted limits come from the best frames.
8. **Unused or limited data.** Gaia epoch astrometry is not public, so the elongation PA comes only from the weak harmonic-phase relation. DES/Legacy Survey and VHS J are saturated, and there is no unsaturated sub-arcsecond imaging.
9. **Previous attempt.** The earlier unfinished run used the same windowing; I re-derived everything in v2 and reproduced its raw offsets exactly, but its interpretation (offsets as positions) is superseded.
10. **Other campaign threads not checked here.** The lcmodel campaign's luminosity and colour inferences were not cross-checked; the colour levers given here are an independent constraint they should be compared against.

summary:
I redid the whole localisation independently in localise/v3. I used my own code throughout and treated the earlier v2 numbers as unverified; they agree with mine.

1. TESS shows a large offset in every sector, but it is a colour effect, not a position offset. In all six sectors the deep eclipses sit 2.0–3.6" from the G star's PRF position, which is 5–6σ against the injection scatter (≈2σ in S1). The direction is always radially away from that sector's camera boresight. I measured an independent effect in the TESS optics from 4,000–5,500 isolated Gaia field stars in six FFIs: redder stars appear shifted away from the boresight by about 1.5" per magnitude of BP−RP, and more steeply for the reddest stars.
   - A fixed sky offset fits the six sectors badly: χ² = 217 for 22 degrees of freedom.
   - An eclipsing source exactly at the G star, with its light redder than the G star, fits well: χ² = 20.8/22, empirical p = 0.50.
   - Fitting position plus colour together gives δ = (dE, dN) = (−0.17 ± 0.18, +0.53 ± 0.28)", i.e. 0.56" at PA 342°. The errors come from injection simulations.
   - δ = 0 is allowed (p = 0.09), and p = 0.69 if S105 is dropped. The offset is under 1.24" at 95% and under 1.48" at 99.7%. Separations of 1.5" or more are excluded at p = 0.002, and 2" or more at p < 0.001.
   - The PA hint (north-northwest) is not significant.
   - The size of the colour shift says the deep-eclipsed star has BP−RP ≈ 2.3 (2.2–2.4), an M1.5–M2.5 dwarf. The shallow-eclipse light is redder still (BP−RP ≳ 3).
   - Injections at 0", 1", 3" and 5" in every sector show biases of at most 0.3" (deep) and scatter of 0.43–0.6" per sector (S1: 0.8–1.5").

2. Gaia's image diagnostics point to an unresolved companion. I calibrated them with about 4,850 imaging-resolved pairs and 6,100 non-detections from SOAR speckle (Tokovinin; Ziegler), Kepler follow-up imaging (Furlan 2017) and Robo-AO, all cross-matched to Gaia DR3.
   - Of 2,650 G = 9–14 non-detections, none matches all four of the target's values together (ipd_frac_multi_peak 30–50, RUWE < 1.4, no Gaia neighbour, BP/RP flagged blended in ≥90% of transits; the target has 47/47 blended).
   - Matching pairs lie at 0.48–1.2" (four full matches at 0.63–1.05") with I-band contrast ΔI ≈ 2–4.7, mostly 3.7–4.7.
   - The harmonic phase gives no position angle at this low amplitude (Rayleigh p = 0.83).

3. Archival imaging. DECam / Legacy Survey cores are saturated (flat-topped). SkyMapper's 5–20 s images are unsaturated but the seeing is 1.8–3.2", only sensitive to Δm ≲ 2–3 at about 1". The VISTA VHS images (ESO cutouts, seeing 1.07–1.36") have saturated cores (radius about 0.7" in Ks, 1.0" in J). Fitting the wings with injection calibration, both Ks pawprints would recover a companion with ΔKs ≤ 2.5 anywhere beyond 0.6" (100%), and ΔKs ≤ 3.0 beyond 1.0". A residual feature at 1.12–1.14", PA 345–350° appears in all three Ks frames but is too faint (ΔKs ≈ 4.0–4.4 after bias correction) to supply the eclipses. Its nature is unconfirmed.

Putting it together: the eclipses come from a red (≈M2) star within about 1.2" of the G star. Its colour and brightness put it at roughly 130–350 pc, consistent with 297 pc. An unrelated star of this kind within 1.24" has a chance probability of about 4×10⁻⁵. A bound triple is strongly favoured.

The self-consistent picture is an M2–M3 + M4–M5 eclipsing pair at about 0.45–0.65" (130–190 au projected), or at most about 1" if ΔKs ≈ 3. It would have ΔKs ≈ 2.5, ΔI ≈ 3.9, ΔG ≈ 5, and about 1.5–3% of the TESS light, so the undiluted primary eclipse is about 25–50% deep. This revises the earlier rough estimate of 6–9% of TESS light, ΔKs 1.5–1.9, 1–1.8", K7+M2: that estimate is excluded by the VHS limits, the TESS separation limits and the measured colour.

conclusions.claim: The eclipsing source lies within about 1.2" of the G star. All resolved Gaia neighbours (18.2", 44–55") and any source at 1.5" or more are excluded.
conclusions.evidence: Joint six-sector fit gives a 95% upper limit of 1.24". Separations ≥1.5" are excluded at p = 0.002 and ≥2" at p < 0.001. The 2" exclusion holds in every variant that includes the deep eclipses (p ≤ 0.005 even with all errors ×1.5).

conclusions.claim: The 2–3.6" raw TESS offsets are a colour effect in the TESS optics, not a real sky offset.
conclusions.evidence: In all six sectors and all three boresight geometries (S105 points the opposite way, S106 is about 60–80° off), the offset points away from the boresight. All 12 tangential components are consistent with zero. The field-star colour coefficient (−1.52 to −1.56"/mag, same sign) explains it. A fixed sky offset gives χ² = 217/22; an on-target red source gives 20.8/22.

conclusions.claim: δ is consistent with zero. The north-northwest offset of about 0.5" is not significant, and TESS gives no meaningful position-angle constraint.
conclusions.evidence: p(δ = 0) = 0.09 (baseline), 0.03–0.69 across variants. Dropping S105 gives (−0.14, +0.24) ± (0.20, 0.45)". The 68% region is PA 301°–11°, but 0" is inside the 95% region.

conclusions.claim: The deep-eclipse light comes from a star with BP−RP ≈ 2.3 (M1.5–M2.5). The shallow-eclipse light is redder (BP−RP ≳ 3). A K7 primary is disfavoured.
conclusions.evidence: Colour shifts c_deep = 2.94 ± 0.28" and c_shallow = 5.34 ± 0.46", ratio 1.82. Read off the red end of the field-star colour curve (BP−RP 2.42 → 3.29"), this gives 2.2–2.4 for the deep eclipse. K7 would predict about 1.35". This depends on the few red calibration stars (about 20 per bin, only 4 beyond 2.7).

conclusions.claim: Gaia DR3 independently indicates a companion at about 0.5–1.2" with I-band contrast about 3.7–4.7 that Gaia did not list as a separate source. The Gaia data give no PA.
conclusions.evidence: No single star matches all four diagnostics (0/2650); matching pairs lie at 0.48–1.2" (four full matches at 0.63–1.05", ΔI 2.0–3.9). The harmonic phase is uninformative at the target's amplitude (Rayleigh p = 0.83, n = 171).

conclusions.claim: A companion as bright as in the earlier rough estimate (ΔKs 1.5–1.9 at 1–1.8", 6–9% of the TESS light) is ruled out.
conclusions.evidence: VHS Ks injections recover ΔKs ≤ 2.0 at ≥ 0.5" (100%) and ΔKs ≤ 2.5 at ≥ 0.6" (100%) in both pawprints. TESS excludes ≥ 1.5". The colour shift excludes a K7 primary.

conclusions.claim: A bound triple is strongly favoured over an unrelated background or foreground eclipsing binary. The most self-consistent picture is an M2–M3 + M4–M5 pair at about 0.45–0.65" (130–190 au), giving about 1.5–3% of the TESS light.
conclusions.evidence: An unrelated M dwarf within 1.24" has a chance probability of about 4×10⁻⁵. The eclipsed star's colour and light fraction put it at about 130–350 pc, consistent with 297 pc. The Gaia lower bound (about 0.48"), VHS upper bound (about 0.6" for ΔKs ≈ 2.5) and TESS limit agree. This relies on approximate main-sequence relations and on undiluted depths of 10–55%.

conclusions.claim: The residual feature in the VHS Ks images (1.12–1.14", PA 345–350°, ΔKs about 4.2) cannot be the eclipsing pair. Whether it is real is unknown.
conclusions.evidence: It appears in all three Ks frames and is much weaker around a matched saturated star (N228). But ΔKs about 4.2 means about 0.5% of the TESS light, which would need eclipses deeper than 100%. Injections show the fit measures companions too bright, not too faint. The two-star comparison test (h03) was inconclusive.

conclusions.claim: Existing seeing-limited imaging cannot resolve the companion.
conclusions.evidence: DECam / Legacy Survey cores are saturated flat (peak fraction 0.003). VHS cores are saturated out to 0.7" in Ks. SkyMapper is unsaturated but the seeing (1.8–3.2") only reaches Δm ≲ 2–3 at about 1".

implications_bound_vs_background:
The evidence now favours a bound hierarchical triple.

1. TESS places the eclipsing light within 1.24" of the G star at 95% (1.48" at 99.7%). This rules out every catalogued Gaia neighbour and any source at 1.5" or more.
2. That light is red: BP−RP ≈ 2.3 for the deep eclipse and redder for the shallow one, i.e. a mid-M primary with a cooler secondary.
3. At this Galactic latitude an unrelated M dwarf of the required brightness lands within 1.24" with probability about 4×10⁻⁵. A bound low-mass companion at 50–370 au is roughly 10³ times more likely a priori.
4. The eclipsed star's photometric distance (about 130–350 pc) brackets the G star's 297 pc.
5. Gaia's image diagnostics independently say there is an unlisted companion at about 0.5–1.2". No single star in the calibration sample matches them (0/2650).
6. VHS shows that a companion bright enough for the earlier rough estimate (ΔKs ≈ 1.5–1.9) would have been seen beyond 0.4–0.5". So the bound eclipsing pair must be fainter (ΔKs ≈ 2.5–3, about 1.5–3% of the TESS light) and closer: about 0.45–0.65" for ΔKs ≈ 2.5, at most about 1.0" for ΔKs ≈ 3. That is about 130–300 au projected.
7. The background interpretation survives only as an unlucky chance alignment within about 1", or a foreground M dwarf if the undiluted eclipse is shallow.

Testable predictions for the follow-up:
- The light-curve modelling should need about 97–98.5% third light (undiluted primary depth about 25–50%).
- 8 m speckle imaging at 562/832 nm (Zorro/'Alopeke) or near-IR adaptive optics should find a companion with Δ(832 nm) ≈ 3.5–4.5 or ΔK ≈ 2.5 at 0.4–0.7". SOAR I-band imaging is borderline.
- Colour-dependent depths in ground photometry should follow an M2+M4–5 eclipsing pair.
caveats:
1. **Colour correction drives the result.** The whole TESS conclusion depends on the colour coefficient of the TESS optics measured from field stars. Its sign and size are well measured (−1.52 to −1.56\"/mag, six sectors, two cameras). But the red end (BP−RP > 2.3) rests on about 20 stars per bin, and only 4 beyond 2.7. That makes the inferred BP−RP of the eclipsed stars uncertain by about ±0.1–0.2 mag, and the shallow-eclipse colour an extrapolation.
2. **The north-northwest offset rests on one sector.** The 0.5\" offset comes mostly from S105, which is camera 2. If that camera's colour effect is stronger for very red sources than its field-star coefficient suggests, δ moves toward 0. Treat the TESS result as an upper limit, not a detection of an offset.
3. **Noise model.** Errors come from real out-of-eclipse fake windows drawn from a shared pool, so trials are not fully independent.
   - The PRF models date from the 2018–19 commissioning; the injections that use the star's own image partly cover any mismatch.
   - The direct-image reference includes the companion's light, so δ is about 2–5% too small, and the colour shifts are about 0.1\" too small.
4. **Gaia calibration limits.**
   - Only 4–11 target-like calibration pairs exist.
   - The calibrators are mostly nearby bright Hipparcos/TOI stars, where orbital motion inflates RUWE. That makes "RUWE < 1.4" more restrictive in the calibration than for a star at 297 pc.
   - Calibrator contrasts are I-band, not G-band. For an M-dwarf companion around a G star, ΔG is about 1–1.5 mag larger than ΔI.
   - I matched the calibrators' primaries as the brightest Gaia source within 4\". This can mis-assign some WDS entries with poor coordinates.
   - The BP/RP blending statistic was calibrated empirically, not from its documented definition.
5. **VHS limits.**
   - The core is saturated out to about 0.7\" in Ks and 1.0\" in J, so the limits inside about 0.5–0.6\" are weak.
   - The detection limits are optimistic because injected companions use the same model PSF as the fit.
   - The 1.1\" residual feature is unexplained; the comparison with the matched star (h03) was inconclusive because of misalignment dipoles in J and Ks2.
   - Only one VHS epoch (2012-08-22) exists, so there is no proper-motion check.
6. **Companion predictions.** The predicted contrasts, light fractions and distances use approximate main-sequence absolute magnitudes and colour conversions that I did not check against a table (about ±0.3 mag). They also assume a near-solar-metallicity M dwarf; the G star's [M/H]_gspphot is −0.35 and flagged unreliable.
7. **Coverage.** S1 (30-min cadence, 1–2 cadences per eclipse) adds little. The S1 shallow-eclipse fit is unstable (planar-background and Gaussian-PSF variants differ by several arcsec), but its injection scatter is 2.4–4.4\", so it carries negligible weight.
8. **Earlier attempt.** I did not reuse v2 results. My code is independent, and its numbers agree closely with v2 (δ (−0.25, +0.51) vs mine (−0.17, +0.53); colour shifts (2.98, 5.53) vs (2.94, 5.34)).
9. **SkyMapper.** The SkyMapper run (h05) was stopped after the g and r images because its sensitivity is irrelevant at the relevant contrasts; its results exist only in the log.
